summary: Ran step M1-S03 of build tier2-webhook with its owning agent apex-builder, executed inline per AGENT.md Step 6's non-Claude-Code clause. The step was in `next`, was claimed `running` at 2026-09-12T10:57:25Z, and the owning agent refused with REFUSAL_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS at its Step 6 template-class provenance check before emitting any file: three of the five templates the step's templates[] mandates cannot be shipped into this build because each references a further templates/apex class whose own custom object or custom metadata type no step of this plan ships. check-outputs reported all 20 declared outputs missing and exited 1, so `built` was unreachable; the step was set `blocked` with reason `ambiguity`, carrying the owning agent's own words into --result. Zero files were written under artefacts/M1-S03/ and nothing outside the build directory was touched. Two remedies are named for a human; neither was applied, and no gate was approved.
confidence_rationale: LOW per this agent's Step 9 table: the step was set `blocked`, and check-outputs reported 20 missing outputs. Every required input of the owning agent resolved from plan.json alone, the step was legitimately in `next`, both envelopes validate, and nothing was written outside artefacts/M1-S03/ - so the LOW is the blocked exit rather than any defect in the run.

The invocation brief restated include_logger and the ApplicationLogger prohibition; both agree with the amended plan record, so nothing was taken from the brief over the plan.
inputs_received.credentials: [REDACTED] - none present. M1-S02's AuthHeader parameterValue is a merge-field reference rather than a key and was not echoed into either envelope.

process_observations.observation: The plan CLI held every line it is supposed to hold: `next` listed M1-S03 and nothing else, set-status running was accepted because M1-S04 being `running` in the same milestone does not block a sibling, set-status blocked required --blocked-reason, and check-outputs refused the `built` transition on its own rather than leaving it to the runner's judgment.

The amendment record on the step made the mid-flight input change auditable without a hand edit: amendments[0] carries the whole prior inputs{} and templates[] block, so the runner could see exactly what changed and why rather than trusting the coordinator's summary of it.

The same defect class has now blocked two of this build's three Apex-touching steps in one morning - M1-S04 on ApplicationLogger, M1-S03 on ApplicationLogger reached through two templates plus TriggerControl reached through a third - which suggests the gap is in what plan-time validation can see rather than in either step.

build_plan.py validate confirms that each path in a step's templates[] exists, and the plan verifier's grounding lens does the same, but neither opens the template file to see which further templates/apex classes or custom metadata types it needs - so a step can cite TriggerHandler without TriggerControl, or HttpClient without ApplicationLogger, and pass every plan-time gate.

process_observations.observation: The runner's Wave 10 persistence contract names docs/reports/build-step-runner/<run_id>.{md,json} as a second, repo-tracked copy of this deliverable, while the invocation constrained writes to the build directory; the build-scoped pair under envelopes/M1-S03/ was written and the docs/reports/ pair was not, which is a divergence a reader of the contract would not predict from the envelope alone.
The remedy is a change to the step's templates[] and inputs, or a new Apex-foundations step, both of which are plan authorship.

Every fact needed is on disk - the templates, their dependencies, and the metadata that would satisfy them all exist in templates/apex/. What is unresolved is which of two bound step inputs wins, which is a plan question for a human.

extensions.concurrency: M1-S04 was `running` under another runner throughout. Nothing under artefacts/M1-S04/ or its envelopes was written, moved or read for anything other than its committed deploy-order.md, which records the same ApplicationLogger finding from its run 1.
extensions.step_inputs_vs_invocation_brief: The brief restated include_logger: false, the ApplicationLogger prohibition and the TestDataFactory duplication. All three agree with the amended plan record, so no divergence had to be reported under Step 5's invocation-is-not-a-source rule. The brief's Step 6 instruction to 'ship every template class you reference verbatim' is what the refusal is about: two of those classes cannot be shipped.
section_3_1_support_gaps: The feature tier's plan shape is 1 milestone and <= 5 steps, with a carve-out only for the aggregating Apex manifest step. Remedy A adds an Apex-foundations step, which section 4's Apex row note explicitly prescribes for a plan with two Apex steps sharing a template dependency - so a correctly-shaped feature-tier plan with two Apex steps needs six, and section 3.1 has no carve-out for it the way it has one for the manifest step. The CLI reports this only as a validate WARN, so the plan reads green.

Neither build_plan.py validate nor the plan verifier's grounding lens reads the body of a cited template, so a templates[] entry that needs a second template or a custom metadata type passes plan time and fails at the builder. Both Apex steps of this build hit it.

The runner's Wave 10 persistence names docs/reports/build-step-runner/<run_id>.{md,json} alongside the build-scoped pair, while the build layer's own section 2 layout puts agent envelopes under envelopes/<step-id>/. The invocation constrained writes to the build directory; the docs/reports/ pair was not written and the divergence is recorded here rather than resolved.
